name: Combat
description: Training, defensive stances and combat interactions. A is the person the move centres on, B their partner; entries give grounded supports, facing and reach.
entries: A stepping backward with knees bent, open hands raised and their weight centered over the rear foot.
A holding a wooden practice sword in both hands above one shoulder, feet staggered and elbows bent.
A kneeling beside a target to retrieve an arrow, bow resting on the ground within reach.

entries.text: A and B circling each other with guarded hands and room between their feet.
A and B pressing padded training shields together, each leaning forward from a planted rear foot.

entries: A bracing a long staff diagonally across their body with both hands spaced apart.
A drawing a sheathed blade with one hand while the other steadies the sheath at their hip.
A seated on a bench, wrapping one hand with a strip held by the other hand.

entries.text: Sword duel: A and B facing each other with staggered feet, each holding a sword forward, their blades meeting between them while their bodies remain apart.
Slip: B throwing a straight punch while A bends their knees and shifts their head outside its path, both keeping their feet grounded.

entries: Archery draw: A standing side-on with feet apart, bow arm extended toward the target and the other hand drawing the string to the cheek, arrow aligned with the bow.

entries.text: Shield block: B advancing with a raised practice weapon while A braces behind a shield, front knee bent and rear foot planted.
Parry: A and B facing each other at arm's length, B extending a practice blade while A redirects it to the side with their own blade.

entries: Boxing guard: A standing with one foot forward, knees slightly bent, fists near the cheeks and elbows close to the ribs.
Front kick: A balancing on one slightly bent leg, extending the other foot forward with their torso upright and hands raised for balance.
Side kick: A balancing on one leg with their torso leaning away, the other leg extended sideways and the heel directed toward the target.
Kneeling guard: A resting one knee on the ground with the other foot planted ahead, holding a shield in front without resting it on the raised knee.

entries.text: Back-to-back defense: A and B standing back-to-back with feet apart, facing opposite directions and each guarding the space in front of them.
Wrist release: A and B facing each other, B gripping A's wrist while A turns their wrist toward the opening between B's thumb and fingers.

entries: A crouching behind low cover with both feet planted, keeping their head below its upper edge while looking around one side.
